name: Speech recognition
plain: Turns the person's speech or audio files into text, possibly on Apple servers.
meaning: Reveals what is said near the phone. iOS warns that audio may go to Apple servers; on-device modes avoid that.

android.prompt_ui: Allow microphone while using, only this time, or don't allow
android.note: Android 13 added an on-device recognizer; Android 17 tightens background audio

ios.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't Allow speech recognition
ios.note: Server mode limited to about 1 minute per request and a daily quota; SpeechAnalyzer is on device

fields.name: maxDuration
fields.range: about 60 per server request on iOS

limits.headline: Can turn your speech into text, sometimes on Apple's servers
limits.user_action: You tap the microphone button and tap Allow for speech recognition
can: Turn your speech or audio files into text
Use on device recognition on Android 13 and later, which stays on the phone
Use Apple's server mode, with a limit of about 1 minute per request and a daily quota (iPhone)
cannot: Use it after you tap Don't Allow
Listen in the background on Android 17 under tighter rules
Keep the audio on the phone when server mode is used on iPhone
limits.differs: Both ask first. iPhone warns that audio may go to Apple's servers. Android 13 and later offers an on device mode.

story.what_it_is: Turns your speech or an audio file into text, sometimes by sending it to Apple's servers.

marketing.name: Speech framework
marketing.pitch: Convert audio to text with on device or server based recognition, after the person agrees.

story.for_you: A pop up says speech might be sent to Apple. After you allow it, you can dictate notes or search with your voice.
story.for_makers: It offers dictation, captions and voice commands without building models. Server mode is stronger but sends audio off device, while on device mode keeps it private.

use_cases.example: You dictate a note and see text appear as you talk.
A video app adds live captions for a hard of hearing viewer.
A word game lets you speak your guess.
A language app listens to your accent and scores it.
Voice control types and taps for someone who cannot use their hands.
You say a command and the app turns it into an action.
You dictate a text message while driving.

risks: Reveals what is said near the phone
story.android_note: Android's SpeechRecognizer may use Google servers, and offline packs can be downloaded.
story.ios_note: iOS warns that audio may go to Apple, and on device mode avoids that.

technical_bounds: Separate mic permission is also required for live audio
Server limits about 1 minute per request

history.change: SpeechAnalyzer for on device long form transcription
